gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patients must have histologically confirmed glioblastoma (or gliosarcoma) at first or second recurrence after initial standard, control or experimental, therapy that includes at least radiation therapy (RT) and temozolomide (TMZ)

candidate_evidence.quote: This trial aims to see if giving a specific thyroid hormone, such as methimazole and liothyronine, is safe and could benefit cancer treatment.
To evaluate the anti-tumor activity of inducing hypothyroxinemic state by assessing progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Inducing a Hypothyroxinemic State in Patients With Recurrent Glioblastoma or Gliosarcoma

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: To evaluate the correlation of PFS and OS with thyroid hormone levels. III. To evaluate the correlation of overall response rate (ORR) with thyroid hormone levels.

role_evidence.quote: Patients receive methimazole orally (PO) daily and lomustine daily.
To evaluate the safety and feasibility of inducing a hypothyroxinemic state in patients with recurrent glioblastoma.
Patients receive liothyronine PO BID to maintain lower free T4 below lower limit of normal and TSH and free T3 in the normal range.

flag.reason: Liothyronine replaces T4 to create hypothyroxinaemia (part of the investigational strategy) but in Category 1 it is given only to correct high TSH, which could be read as supportive.

role_evidence.quote: Treatment with lomustine repeats every 6 weeks for up to 6 cycles or 12 months.

agents.drug_class_hint: nitrosourea alkylating agent, established GBM therapy

coder_notes: EARLY_PHASE1 (translational subset). Investigational strategy is drug-induced hypothyroxinaemia (methimazole and/or liothyronine depending on baseline thyroid category) on a lomustine backbone given to all patients. Both thyroid-modulating drugs coded experimental_combination since the Category 1 regimen gives methimazole plus liothyronine; in Categories 2/3 liothyronine is the sole investigational drug. Target engagement coded yes because serum thyroid hormone levels (the intended pharmacodynamic effect) are measured and correlated with outcome; thyroid hormone levels are not tumour biomarkers and are not listed. Methimazole INN is thiamazole.
